title: ר' נתן הבבלי

paragraphs:
R. Natan the Babylonian, Mishnah Berakhot 9:5; Shekalim 2:5. (a) Scribe and court head in Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's academy, Rabbi's father. R. Meir's colleague (see Meir’s entry for why R. Natan was called ‘Some say’). 'Some say': Avodah Zarah 15; Shevuot 35b; Ḥullin 80a; Pesaḥim 29a; Menaḥot 76b; Bava Batra 15b. Tosafot there says that 'Some say' is not R. Natan; also Shenei Luḥot HaBerit 409b. A judge penetrating to law's depths, Bava Kamma 53a; Bava Metzia 117b; Rashi calls him court head. All his ancestors were Babylonian exilarchs; see Arukh: his father was exilarch, and R. Natan went up to the Land and became court head. Elijah spoke with him, telling him to eat a third, drink a third and leave a third, so that when you grow angry, you will be no more than full, Gittin 70a. Bava Metzia 59b, R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua's oven of Akhnai: R. Natan met Elijah (see his entry). He traveled to overseas towns, Cappadocia, where children died after circumcision. Seeing they were greenish, he told them to wait; circumcised afterward, they lived and were named Natan the Babylonian after him, Shabbat 134a; Ḥullin 47b; Shir HaShirim Rabbah, 'How beautiful are your steps.'

(b) Shemuel Yarḥina'ah saw the book of Adam the first human [the Warsaw text reads ארה״ר], containing 'Rabbi and R. Natan, end of Mishnah,' Bava Metzia 86. R. Natan told Rabbi, 'You taught your Mishnah according to R. Yoḥanan ben Berokah,' etc. Rabbi said he had been childish and brazen toward Natan the Babylonian. Rashbam: childish foolishness, rejecting him with something insubstantial, Bava Batra 131a. Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubbot 4, halakhah 12: R. Zeira in R. Yoḥanan's name says Rabbi asked Natan why they ruled like R. Yoḥanan ben Berokah: 'Did you not teach us?' He came to his father, who told him, “You wronged Natan the Babylonian”. See Tosafot Menaḥot 44a, 'To R. Ḥiyya's study house.'

(c) He was Babylonian, Gittin 65b. Bava Batra 73a: R. Natan the Babylonian called it butzit; Sumkhos of the Land called it dugit. Ketubbot 52a: R. Natan says he asked Sumkhos. (d) He made many books, such as mishnayot and Avot deRabbi Natan. (e) Toledot Adam VeḤavvah, the eminent Yeruḥam bar Meshullam, Ḥavvah, Yibbum and Ḥalitzah, part 3, quotes Ramah: between Rabbi and R. Natan the law follows R. Natan. Although Rabbi prevails against his colleague, R. Natan differed, being Rabbi's teacher and his father's teacher. Yuḥasin writes this in Seder HaDorot. This requires examination: Rabbi’s father was nasi, and R. Natan was head of the court. גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael] places R. Natan's grave at Pumbedita; I do not know whether it is this Natan. Benjamin's Travels places R. Natan and R. Naḥman, Rav Pappa's sons, there.

(h [source lettering]) Rav Adda son of R. Shimon in his name. Others say in R. Natan's name, Tosefta Ma'aserot 2. R. Dosa, Eruvin 83. R. Ḥanina ben Uri in R. Natan's name. R. Ḥanina fell ill; R. Natan visited him, Ḥullin 47b. Ḥananyah, son of R. Yehoshua's brother (see his entry). R. Yoshiyah (see his entry). In R. Yose the Galilean's name (see above); in Abba Yose of Meḥoza's name. R. Yaakov said, Gittin 14b. R. Yitzḥak in R. Natan's name, in R. Yose the Galilean's name, in R. Yoḥanan ben Nuri's name, Menaḥot 38b. Yonatan HaKitoni disagrees with him. In R. Yishmael's name, Pesaḥim 67b; Niddah 43b. R. Yishmael son of R. Yose in his name. R. Yishmael bar R. Naḥman said: R. Natan said. R. Meir, his colleague (see above). R. Matya ben Ḥarash addressed him as 'My teacher,' Avot deRabbi Natan 1. R. Natan bar Shila testified in his name. Sumkhos (see above). R. Simon in R. Natan's name, Vayikra Rabbah 10. R. Natan said, 'Not what R. Akiva said,' Shevuot 6b; Menaḥot 83b, R. Natan and R. Akiva. Rav and R. Natan, one says, etc., Af Al Pi 55a. Rabbi, his student (see above). Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel (see above).
